target_customer: Enterprise teams and developers that automate business processes and need business users to manage decision rules
problem: Workflow and automation tools handle logic badly: rules get complicated, process owners cannot edit them and need specialist services. Rulebricks separates decision logic into a spreadsheet like interface exposed as APIs.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free tier, plus self hosted and on premises deployment options
product_category: No code business rules engine and decision management

founders.name: Sid Garimella
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in finance infrastructure for a few years and now focuses on automation; employers not named.

technical_complexity.rationale: A low latency rules evaluation engine with a visual decision table editor and versioning; moderate engineering for a solo founder.

defensibility.rationale: Rules stored and called through APIs create some lock in, but rule engines are a mature category with open source options.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; the company appears independent and still active with SOC 2 Type II.

market_need_then: The founder's YC application described five figure RPA platforms as the alternative and workflow tools whose logic steps get complicated, as stated on the YC page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, enterprise trust oriented with tagline Make decisions anywhere

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive compound name that hints at building blocks of rules, but no press or community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Rulebricks stayed a very small team with a decision management product aimed at enterprises and now cites Fortune 500 customers and SOC 2 Type II. No public funding, exit or shutdown was found, so the trajectory beyond the YC investment is not documented.
notes: Competitors: two dated searches found no contemporaneous rival sources near March 2021, so the list is empty; SaaShub lists DecisionRules and GoRules but those lists are undated and DecisionRules raised only in 2025. CB Insights shows a 500K convertible note from Y Combinator dated January 2021; one aggregator only, so not recorded as a round. Founder education and employers not found. Company site and YC page do not name other founders.
